questions.q: $(p\vee q)\wedge(p\vee r)$ என்ற மெய் அட்டவணையில் உள்ள நிரைகளின் எண்ணிக்கை :
$*$ என்ற ஈருறுப்புச் செயலி $a*b=\dfrac{ab}{7}$ என வரையறுக்கப்படுகிறது. $*$ எதன் மீது ஈருறுப்புச் செயலி ஆகாது ?
questions.solution: On $\mathbb Z$, $1*1=\dfrac17\notin\mathbb Z$, so $*$ is not a binary operation on $\mathbb Z$.

questions.q: கழித்தலின் கீழ் பின்வரும் கணம் அடைவு பெறவில்லை :
questions.solution: $1-2=-1\notin\mathbb N$, so subtraction is not a binary operation on $\mathbb N$.

questions.q: The number of binary operations that can be defined on a set with 2 elements is :
questions.solution: A binary operation assigns one of 2 values to each of the $2\times2=4$ ordered pairs: $2^4=16$.

questions.q: The identity element for multiplication on $\mathbb R$ is :
The conditional $p\to q$ is false only when :
questions.solution: A conditional fails only when a true hypothesis leads to a false conclusion.

questions.q: Which of the following is a tautology ?
questions.solution: $p\vee\neg p$ is true whatever the truth value of $p$.

questions.q: In $(\mathbb Z_5,\times_5)$, the inverse of $[2]$ is :
How many rows are there in the truth table of a statement with 4 simple statements?
In $(\mathbb Z_7,+_7)$, find the inverse of $[3]$ (give the representative between $0$ and $6$).
On $\mathbb Z$, define $a*b=a+b-3$. Find the identity element.
On $\mathbb Q\setminus\{-1\}$, define $a*b=a+b+ab$. Find the inverse of $2$, correct to three decimal places.
How many commutative binary operations can be defined on a set with 2 elements?
questions.solution:
A commutative operation is fixed by its values on the unordered pairs $\{a,a\}$, $\{a,b\}$, $\{b,b\}$: $3$ of them.

Each takes one of $2$ values: $2^3=8$.

questions.q: Using truth tables, show that $p\to q\equiv\neg p\vee q$, and that $(p\wedge q)\to p$ is a tautology.
questions.solution:
**Part 1.** Columns: $p$, $q$, $p\to q$, $\neg p$, $\neg p\vee q$.

**Row 1:** T, T — $p\to q$ = T; $\neg p\vee q$ = F ∨ T = T

**Row 2:** T, F — $p\to q$ = F; $\neg p\vee q$ = F ∨ F = F

**Row 3:** F, T — $p\to q$ = T; $\neg p\vee q$ = T ∨ T = T

**Row 4:** F, F — $p\to q$ = T; $\neg p\vee q$ = T ∨ F = T

The last two columns agree in every row, so $p\to q\equiv\neg p\vee q$.

**Part 2.** Columns: $p$, $q$, $p\wedge q$, $(p\wedge q)\to p$.

**Row 1:** T, T — $p\wedge q$ = T; T → T = T

**Row 2:** T, F — $p\wedge q$ = F; F → T = T

**Row 3:** F, T — $p\wedge q$ = F; F → F = T

**Row 4:** F, F — $p\wedge q$ = F; F → F = T

Every entry of the last column is T, so $(p\wedge q)\to p$ is a tautology.
